results.text:
Response deadline
Evidence must be sent at least one business day before the card network deadline. The card network deadline shows up in the dispute's deadline field, and the Acme Payments internal cutoff is one business day before it. A response sent after the card network deadline loses the dispute automatically, with no review of the merits. When the deadline falls on a Monday, the internal cutoff is the Friday before.

When to escalate
A dispute must be escalated to a human analyst when the card network deadline is 2 days away or less, when the internal cutoff has already passed, when the amount exceeds 5,000 or when required evidence is missing. The full criteria are in the escalation and review policy.

When to escalate
Escalate the case to a human analyst when there are claims contradicted by the evidence, when missing data prevents a conclusion, when a dispute deadline is 2 days away or less, or when any amount involved is above 5,000. A single one of these criteria is enough to make human review mandatory.

Deadline close
A dispute with the card network deadline 2 days away or less has critical urgency. If the internal cutoff, which is one business day before the card network deadline, has already passed, the case needs a human decision on the same day. The system reports the days left, the internal cutoff and the evidence still missing.

What to tell the customer
The answer to the customer confirms that there were two equal charges within a short interval and states which one will be returned, the amount, the currency and the deadline of up to 5 business days. The answer blames neither the customer nor the merchant. If the duplicate was not confirmed, the answer explains why and asks for more information.

Response times
Critical cases must be seen by a person on the same business day. High urgency cases, within 1 business day. Normal cases, within 3 business days. Low urgency cases can wait in the regular queue. These times count from the moment the case is escalated, not from the moment the customer wrote.

Dispute stages
A dispute goes through stages in order. In `opened`, the card network announced it was opened. In `evidence_requested`, Acme asked the merchant for evidence. In `evidence_submitted`, the evidence was sent to the card network. In `won` or `lost`, the card network decided for or against the merchant. A resolved dispute never goes back to an earlier stage.

Refunds and disputes
A payment with an open chargeback cannot be refunded at the same time, because the customer would get paid twice. While the dispute is open, the refund request waits for the outcome. If the merchant wins the dispute, the payment goes back to being a normal captured payment and the request can be reviewed again.
